behavior_constraints: A target with `matrix = {key: [vals], ...}` is expanded into one concrete target per cartesian-product combination
${key} placeholders in name, command, dependencies, inputs, outputs, and env values are replaced with matrix values
Duplicate expanded target names across the pipeline cause exit 1 with an error message
Other targets may reference expanded target names as dependencies
matrix_include entries are appended to the cartesian product; combinations already present are not duplicated
matrix_exclude entries are partial maps; any combination matching all keys in any exclude entry is dropped
Processing order is: cartesian product, then include, then exclude
matrix_include entries must specify exactly the same keys as the matrix; otherwise exit 1
Matrix substitution runs before pipeline variable expansion so ${key} resolves to the matrix value, never a same-named pipeline variable
entities.summary: This round adds matrix expansion to targets via matrix/matrix_include/matrix_exclude with ${key} substitution applied before pipeline variable expansion, requiring uniqueness of expanded names and integrating expanded targets into dependency resolution.

instruction_head: Add matrix expansion. A target can have `matrix = {key = ["val1", "val2"], ...}`. The target is expanded into one concrete target per cartesian-product combination, replacing `${key}` in `name`, `command`, `dependencies`, `inputs`, `outputs`, and `env` values. Expanded names must be unique across all targets -- exit 1 with an error if not. Non-matrix targets stay as-is. Other targets can depend on expanded names.
